events.title: The Bowery Presents Liana Flores
about: Doors open at 7:00 PM · Show begins at 8:00 PM
“This record is the story of the country girl moving to the city,” Liana Flores says. “It’s bossa nova meets pop, inspired by the people, relationships and glamour of city life.”

Since the release of her acclaimed 2024 debut album Flower of the soul, British-Brazilian singer-songwriter Liana Flores has been at the forefront of a bossa nova revival. Drawing on the ‘60s sound of genre pioneers like Joao Gilberto alongside pop songwriting, Flores combines the dual aspects of her cultural heritage to create an emotive sound.

Following extensive tour dates across North America, Asia and Europe, Flores now returns with a new EP, And so it goes…, that expands her palette to encompass the playful and ebullient experiences of moving from her rural hometown in Norfolk to St. Andrews before coming to London. The result is a six track collection that shifts between finger-picked guitar and gossamer bossa vocals of “So it goes” to the upbeat funk inflections of the heavy-grooving love song “So mysterious”, the Carole King-influenced folk storytelling of “Here to stay,” and the sprightly, glittering pop melodies of “Silvershoes.”

“These songs were informed by my experiences living in the city and touring for the first time. I grew up and studied in small towns with nature in my surroundings, so that’s what came naturally in terms of lyrics. With So it goes, the lyrics are more centred on human connection, and I wanted to explore a part of my identity that’s more playful and matter-of-fact. I also wanted to challenge myself to write songs with strong melodies that would be fun to sing or to get ready to.”

Raised by an immigrant Brazilian mother and British father in East Anglia, Flores first began learning music while listening to ‘80s and ‘90s bossa nova artists like Bebel Gilberto and Leila Pinheiro alongside Top 40 pop radio. In her late teens, she picked up a guitar and started emulating finger-picked bossa nova guitar chords by ear, first covering Tom Jobim standards, then writing her own songs combining the bossa guitar style with her own introspective lyrics, expressing loneliness, self-doubt, and endurance.

“Music is the way I best communicate and connect with the world, through the listener, collaboration with fellow musicians, and the guidance of my musical forbears. I'm particularly drawn to the use of sophisticated…

about: Tito Puente Jr. comes to Arts at the Armory’s Spotlight Series on Friday, December 11, 2026!

The heir to the "King of Mambo," continues his passionate mission to nurture his father's magnificent Latin jazz and salsa legacy. Tito Puente, Jr. has made a name for himself as one of the most exciting Latin musicians touring today. Tito Puente Jr. carries his father with him – imprinted on his physical being and locked in his soul. It’s in his looks, his joy, and his music. Tito Jr. is on a passionate mission, determined to nurture the musical legacy left by his father.

He has found captive audiences who echo his passion. Crowds lured to a venue by the father are returning to see the son — and to once again participate in the high voltage celebration that takes place on stage and spills onto the dance floor.

Tito Puente, Jr. and his ensemble brings exhilarating Latin rhythms that will get your feet moving. They will be joined by dancers and musicians from MetaMovements who will energize an immersive evening that will begin with complimentary dance lessons when doors open. The evening will continue with an opening set by MetaMovements’ Conjunto Obaye and their unique blend of Cuban music designed for dancing, including Afro-Cuban, Rumba, Salsa and Son. With one foot in Boston and the other in the Caribbean, MetaMovements is an artist collective advancing community engagement and well-being through music, dance and participatory cultural events.
This concert will be proudly co-presented by Ágora Cultural Architects.

events.title: JGB Tribute, The Diamond Blues
about: Diamond Blues, delivers high-energy, soulful, and exploratory performances in tribute to the one-of-a-kind, rock-gospel-soul-rhythm and blues group, Jerry Garcia Band.
Since 2021, Diamond Blues, an eclectic group of accomplished musicians passionate about honoring the legacy of Jerry Garcia, have taken New England by storm.

Led by David Rubin on Vocals & Guitar, Diamond Blues features Robbie Parrish on Drums, Ian Brenkle on Bass, Caroline Killoh on Vocals & Keys, and Christopher Belden on Sax and backing vocals. An ensemble capable of furnishing any era of the Jerry Garcia Band story.

DB, as it’s often called by fans, mines their repertoire from the Jerry Garcia Band songbook and blends other fan favorites consistent with the original sound of JGB. Their uniquely crafted setlists touch the entire catalogs of JGB, Legion of Mary/Merl Saunders, and Jerry Garcia Solo, leaving audiences inspired and electrified. DB blends deep cuts with hits that will have you respectfully asking, “why didn’t Jerry play that more often?”
$17 in advance. $22 at the door.

events.title: Magen Tracy and the Missed Connections, Eric Salt & The Electric City
about: Eric Salt & The Electric City are best known for their energenic live shows. Drummer/ brother Denis Saulnier, bassist Eric Anderson, and guitarist Mike Oram have been playing together for decades. Keyboardist and vocalist Magen Tracy joined the band in 2024 adding even more uniqueness to their live shows. The band's records are anthem rock soundscapes combining indie rock infuences (Replacements, Soul Asylum, Pleasure Club) with more traditional rock (Stones, Dylan). “It’s the type of track that you’ll recognize for the rest of your life after only hearing it once.” -Vanyaland Magen Tracy & the Missed Connections - With a catalog that ranges from pop effervescence to alt-country grit—with plenty of rock in between—Magen Tracy & the Missed Connections are a Boston-area favorite known for earworm, melodies, sharp lyrical play, and fun, often mischievous live shows. Led by songwriter Tracy, a three-time Boston Music Award nominee, the band’s piano-driven songs, tight harmonies, and feminist edge take inspiration from acts like Jenny Lewis, Brandi Carlile, and Fleetwood Mac—all backed by a top-notch band that includes Stud Green on violin and guitar, Tamora Gooding on drums, Mike Oram on guitar, and Sam Spencer on bass. Tracy (keys, guitar) has also played in other notable acts, including Letters to Cleo, Kay Hanley, Juliana Hatfield, and Band of Their Own. Her latest single, “At My Age,” is garnering rave reviews, with Tanya Donelly (Belly, Throwing Muses) calling it “powerful and brave.”

Lavelle writes music that feels lived-in and unguarded, shaping raw, honest melodies and textured soundscapes that draw listeners closer and offer a sense of shared experience.

Lavelle will be backed by her band and additional musicians featured on the album, including Mickey Roache on pedal steel, mandolin, and guitar; Tom Murray on drums and vocals; Ed Newton on bass and guitar; Robert Sevigny on guitar and vocals; Greg Hurren on bass; Bob Adams and Neil Kay on saxophone.

about: Voices of Ireland brings together three of Ireland’s finest performers — Don Stiffe, Ger O’Donnell and Trevor Sexton — in a powerful celebration of Irish music, song and storytelling.

about: Which Side?: A Protest Music Teach-Out is a concert and discussion series celebrating and exploring protest music.

The events uses James Sullivan’s book, Which Side Are You On?: 20th Century American History in 100 Protest Songs, as a starting point for the presentation of songs that ask listeners to consider how music gives voice to resistance, advocacy, and change. While the series will anchor itself to the book, collaborators will also contribute 21st-century music, both originals and covers.

events.title: Brian O'Donovan Legacy Series: Revels Chantey Sing with David Coffin
about: Join Revels Artist-in-Residence and master chantey man David Coffin for an evening of chanteys and sea songs. We’ll explore the history and traditions of sea chanteys the way we know best – by singing them! This is an audience participation event, and song sheets will be provided. We can’t wait to sing on the high seas with you!

David Coffin has performed throughout New England since 1980. He is widely known for his rich baritone voice and his impressive collection of musical instruments, which includes concertinas, recorders, penny-whistles, bombards, gemshorns, cornamuse, shawm, rauschphieffe – or, as he explains, “generally anything that requires a lot of hot air”. At the heart of David’s work is his extensive collection of songs from the Maritime tradition. To date, David has recorded four solo CDs; his latest, Last Trip Home, was released in the Fall of 2009 and features his daughter, Linnea, who is also a Revels performer.

David has performed with Revels since 1980 as a singer, instrumentalist and, since 1991, as Master of Ceremonies. Since 2014, David has served as Artist in Residence at Revels and has presented his acclaimed School Enrichment Programs to schools across the region as an extension of Revels Education. He runs tours of Boston Harbor during the summer months, leading over 5,000 inner-city children on boat trips to George’s and Spectacle Islands. He also directs the narration program for Boston Harbor Cruises and hosts the Brunch Cruises every weekend from May to October.

events.title: The Dambuilders - TWO SHOWS with Special Guests
about: The Dambuilders' inventive blend of indie rock, pop, and electric violin earned them a devoted following on college radio in the 1990s. Originally formed in Honolulu, the band relocated to Boston in 1990 and went on to release six albums, including three for Elektra Records, tour extensively throughout North America, Europe, and Australia, and share stages with artists including Lush, Luna, Jeff Buckley, Weezer, Everclear, and others. Their acclaimed 1994 album Encendedor featured “Shrine,” named one of MTV’s 100 Greatest Songs of the ’90s, Lollapalooza edition. The Dambuilders reunited in 2025, performing their 1989 debut in its entirety, and returned with “Shrine 2026,” their first new release in decades, accompanied by a new song, “I Hope We’re Not Too Late.” The new lineup includes original members Dave Derby, Kevin March, and Eric Masunaga, along with guitarist Sean Eden (Luna) and violinist Claudia Chopek (Father John Misty, TV on the Radio).

November 20th - Special Guests Sleepyhead Sleepyhead was formed in a basement room at NYU's Brittany dorm in the fall of 1989 by drummer/vocalist Rachael McNally, bassist Mike Galinsky and guitarist/vocalist Chris O’Rourke. They released their first 7" single, the Kramer-produced "Play," in 1991, and six full-length albums followed: Punk Rock City USA (Slumberland 1993), Starduster (Homestead 1994), Communist Love Songs (Homestead 1996), The Brighter Shore (Sealed Fate 1999), Wild Sometimes (Carrot Top 2014), and New Alchemy (Wild Sometimes Records 2022). After signing to Dromedary Records in 2025, the current lineup of Chris O’Rourke, Rachael McNally, Derek van Beever, and Ani Somasundaram released the 7” single “Hoping That You’re Lonely” b/w “Busted Lullaby.” They are currently working with producer Jon Lupfer on their seventh album at Q Division Studios in Cambridge, MA for release in 2027. Their new songs conjure the subtly infectious laissez-faire sounds of pre-Grunge Indie Rock they embraced early on in their career as well as evoking classic Laurel Canyon Country-Rock and other 70’s FM staples.

November 21st - Hilken & Melissa Band Hilken & Melissa Band features two original members of Fuzzy, the ’90s indie rock band signed to Atlantic Records and featured in Rolling Stone for writing one of the Top 50 Songs of the Decade. The band includes Hilken Mancini (Fuzzy, Shepherdess, The Monsieurs) and Melissa…

Their new songs conjure the subtly infectious laissez-faire sounds of pre-Grunge Indie Rock they embraced early on in their career as well as evoking classic Laurel Canyon Country-Rock and other 70’s FM staples.

November 21st - Hilken & Melissa Band Hilken & Melissa Band features two original members of Fuzzy, the ’90s indie rock band signed to Atlantic Records and featured in Rolling Stone for writing one of the Top 50 Songs of the Decade. The band includes Hilken Mancini (Fuzzy, Shepherdess, The Monsieurs) and Melissa…

events.title: Makis Emmanouilidis - CD Release Concert
about: Makis Emmanouilidis is a Boston-based Greek singer-songwriter and founder of MIA ANASA. Since 1997 he has performed throughout New England, including appearances at MIT's Kresge Auditorium, the Tsai Performance Center, and the Maliotis Cultural Center. His original music combines the rich traditions of Greek folk and rebetiko with contemporary influences. His latest album, Meeting Point, reflects his passion for building cultural bridges through original songs that honor Greek musical heritage while speaking to today's audiences.

events.title: Hollow Harvest
about: Autumn Hollow blends raw rock energy with thoughtful Americana storytelling, led by frontman Brendan Murphy's distinctive vocals and incisive songwriting. With Mike Burke's textured lead guitar work and the dynamic rhythm section of Chuck Vath (bass) and Ian McMillan (drums), the band has become a fixture in the New England music scene through performances at venues like The Paradise Rock Club and Club Passim. Drawing from diverse influences spanning Bob Dylan to hip hop, Murphy crafts songs that feel both familiar and surprising. His background as a teacher brings lived experience to lyrics that often tackle social themes with nuance and insight. Their previous EP, Throw the House, earned Boston Music Award nominations and praise from the Boston Globe for their "unalloyed rock 'n roll." Known for live shows that balance jam band spontaneity with tightly crafted songs, Autumn Hollow creates music that respects tradition without being constrained by it. Their album Say No More represents a significant evolution in their sound—one that embraces experimentation while remaining accessible and emotionally resonant.

Nate Perry & Ragged Company - After leaving the Army in 2018, frontman Nate Perry returned to the Boston area with a new mission: to start a band. Stationed near Nashville, Perry had initially focused on a military career, but his time in Kentucky and Tennessee reignited his long-held passion for music. During his time off, he immersed himself in Nashville's live music scene, captivated by the musicians on stage who were living the dream he longed to pursue. Back in Boston, Nate soon connected with guitarist Mike Chandler, a seasoned player whose previous band had recently disbanded. Together, they began shaping a new musical direction. To complete the lineup, they brought in drummer Sam Demello, bassist Connor Milligan, and keyboardist Ollie Nash. This collaboration birthed Nate Perry & Ragged Company, a dynamic new force in the Americana-rock scene. Since forming, Nate Perry & Ragged Company have been lighting up the Boston music scene and beyond, playing shows that highlight their infectious songwriting and electric guitar-driven sound. In 2024, they released their debut EP, "The Otherside of Everything," which rapidly garnered over 10,000 streams, a testament to their growing popularity. Nate Perry's journey from the Army to concert stages is a…

events.title: Brian O’Donovan Legacy Series: Frankie Gavin
about: Frankie Gavin has played fiddle and flute since his teenage years. At the age of seventeen, he won All-Ireland competitions for fiddle and flute. Originally influenced by the great Irish and American-Irish fiddle players, James Morrison, andMichael Coleman, he later found himself playing with the stars including among others The Rolling Stones, Earl Scruggs, Lez Paul, Stéphane Grappelli, James Galway and Yehudi Menuhin as well as with many of the great contemporary players and singers of traditional Irish music. All have left their mark on his eclectic approach to music. In 2010, he officially became the world’s fastest fiddle player when he played The Foxhunter’s Reel, at a breath-taking 150 beats per minute!

Gavin has played for four American presidents,starting, at the age of six when he played for John F. Kennedy on his 1962 visit to Ireland, then later for Presidents Clinton, Bush and Obama. He has also played for France’s President Mitterrand, Britain’s Prince Charles (now King Charles III), Prince Albert of Monaco and, in front of the Pope on his last visit to Ireland.

The name Frankie Gavin is also synonymous with De Dannan, the globally renowned traditional Irishband he founded in the mid-1970s. Despite a few breaks and changes of personnel over the years, the band continues to play still performs and excites audiences in Ireland and around the world.

Another of Gavin’s recent projects is The Princess Grace Symphonic Suite, composed by Frankie and arranged by Carl Hession, was performed in Monaco with the Monte Carlo Philharmonic Orchestra in September 2022 in front Princess Grace’s son, Prince Albert. It is expected that the suite will performed in Ireland, the USA and elsewhere in the future.
There is more information about Frankie Gavin together with videos and audio tracks on this website dedannan.irish

events.title: Hot Start
about: Boston rock scene – get ready for a night where alternative meets raw indie jam-rock. Hot Start will crank the energy into overdrive with youthful grit, ripping guitar, and electric chaos from their repertoire of indie classics (The Strokes, The Beatles, The Backseat Lovers, etc.) and originals.

events.title: Alice Howe & Freebo
about: Alice Howe & Freebo have undeniable chemistry. Rock bass legend Freebo weaves his fretless stylings into Alice’s soulful, impeccably-tuned vocals for a harmony-driven performance showcasing two uniquely compelling songwriters.

Freebo is a genuine folk, rock, and blues icon who has toured and recorded with some of the greatest artists of his generation, and is best known for his ten years as bassist with Bonnie Raitt. His fretless bass can be heard on records by John Mayall, Ringo Starr, Crosby Stills & Nash, Maria Muldaur, Joe Walsh, Dr. John, and many more. Freebo is also a multi award-winner and finalist in numerous songwriting contests, was recognized as Best Folk Artist by the Los Angeles Music Awards, and has appeared on Saturday Night Live, The Muppet Show, The Midnight Special, and in concert with the Legendary Spinal Tap.

Alice Howe had the honor of being named Best Female Artist at the International Acoustic Music Awards. To hear her sing is to be enraptured by the natural, unaffected beauty of her voice. There’s no artifice, no histrionics — just honest, authentic, emotionally resonant singing in the tradition of the roots music that shaped her. Her poetic lyrics and melodic sensibilities take center stage on her latest solo album Circumstance, produced by Freebo and recorded at legendary FAME Studios in Muscle Shoals, AL. Americana Highways writes of Circumstance: “One of 2023’s best albums. This isn’t just a singer – this is an artist.”

Alice & Freebo have been working as a duo since 2017, and together they tour relentlessly, playing over 85 shows annually in both 2024 and 2025 across US and Europe. “A beguiling blend of folk, rock, blues, and soul,” their collaboration reveals a deep musical kinship that transcends their generational divide. Their latest album Alice Howe & Freebo Live debuted as the #1 Most Played Album on the Folk Radio Charts, and also landed on its Top Ten Albums of 2025.

“Together, on stage, Howe and Freebo are the perfect fit.” - Americana UK “When these two get together, prepare yourself for an extraordinary evening of song and smiles, and maybe a tear or two. Powerful songwriting, mesmerizing vocals, outstanding musicianship, and a palpable camaraderie make for an experience unsurpassed on the contemporary acoustic scene.” - The Folk Music Notebook $30 in advance. $35 at the door.
This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 6pm.…

events.title: Say Darling
about: Say Darling is back for their annual Thanksgiving show at The Buren! The band is bringing the full quintet back for this holiday tradition, don't miss it this year!
Sometimes, what you were looking for comes right when you're not looking at all. You might say that's how Say Darling was formed.
In 2016,old friends Celia Woodsmith and Chris Hersch found themselves taking a step back from their international touring projects.

Grammy-Nominated singer and songwriter Celia Woodsmith – of the acclaimed bluegrass band Della Mae – and critically lauded guitarist Chris Hersch of the alt. country rock band Girls Guns & Glory, had each independently decided to relax their rigorous schedules, both ending up back home in New England with time on their hands.

events.title: 5th Sunday Honky Tonk Dance Party with The Beantown Buckaroos
about: The Beantown Buckaroos cook up classic Western Swing and Country music, with a dash of Tex-Mex and Cajun for picante. You could say we play both kinds of music, Country and Western.

The Bucks were born when a few vets of Boston’s roots community got to powwow with some cowboys new to town, all of us steeped in the music of the great American Southwest, from Bob Wills, Merle Travis, and vintage honky-tonk, to contemporaries like Doug Sahm, Asleep at the Wheel, and The Hot Club of Cowtown.

With four vocalists and six instruments—including fiddle, accordion and pedal steel—the Bucks deliver just the right mix of tight harmonies, driving rhythms, and great repertoire to deliver you to the dance floor, smiling.
2-step dance lesson included at 7pm before the show begins.
$20 in advance. (+Service fees applied at checkout)
Special "2FER" advanced pricing: 2 for $30!
$25 at the door (no 2fers! Get'm in advance!)
This Is An All Ages Show
Doors 6pm · 2 Step Dance lesson 7pm
Showtime is about 7:30, after the lesson.
Dinner and drinks available at all tables but seating is limited as we moved tables out for our dance floor. Come early for dinner and get a table!

events.title: Brian O’Donovan Legacy Series: Annual Holiday Benefit Variety Show
about: The Friday Café, a weekly daytime drop-in program in Harvard Square, offers a welcoming space where homeless and housed adults can gather and get to know each other. Serving an average of 100 guests a week, it offers food and coffee, rest and resources to people living on the margins—but most importantly, community. At the Friday Café, people experiencing a wide variety of life circumstances can relax, share a meal, and talk together as friends.
$40 Advance (+ processing fees). · Doors 5:30/Show time 7:30

events.title: Brian O’Donovan Legacy Series: An Irish Christmas with JOHN DOYLE, CATHIE RYAN & MICK MCAULEY
about: John Doyle and Mick McAuley’s nearly telepathic musical connection began in the truly groundbreaking Irish-American band, Solas. For over thirty-five years, including multiple studio recordings, musical collaborations, and awards, Cathie Ryan has been in the vanguard of Irish music. Now, these three luminaries of Irish music come together to celebrate the Christmas and winter holidays with an evening of exquisite traditional and contemporary songs, tunes, and stories fitting of the season. From familiar carols to special ones that are less well known, as well as new material and their own personal holiday stories, An Irish Christmas with John Doyle, Cathie Ryan and Mick McAuley is a beautiful and evocative evening from these three stellar artists.

John Doyle’s influences include well-known English folk singers Nic Jones, Martin Carthy, Richard Thompson and The Watersons; Scottish singers Dick Gaughan and John Martin; fellow Irishmen Paul Brady and Al O’Donnell; and his father, Sean Doyle—probably the biggest influence of all. Having started his professional career at the age of 16, John went on to form the highly acclaimed supergroup, Solas, with Seamus Egan, John Williams, Karan Casey and Winifred Horan, which took the folk and Celtic music worlds by storm, in no small part due to John’s powerhouse rhythmic guitar style and innovative arrangements. Since then, John’s flourishing solo career, highly regarded solo albums, and in-demand studio prowess as producer have made him one of the busiest artists in all of traditional music. He is a Grammy-nominated artist for his 2009 recording with fiddler Liz Carroll, “Double Play”, has performed at the White House, was music director for folk music legend Joan Baez, guitarist for Mary Chapin Carpenter, and has recorded and/or performed with a who’s who of folk, Celtic, bluegrass and old-time music, including Tim O’Brien, Kate Rusby, Eileen Ivers, Karan Casey, Rodney Crowell and Jerry Douglas. John’s original rhythmic and percussive guitar style has been emulated by guitarists all over the world.

Cathie Ryan has built a loyal following by touring internationally and singing “songs of the heart” at performing arts centers, festivals, folk clubs, and with symphony orchestras. Cathie is a captivating performer whose shows are renowned for their intimacy and power – and a typically Irish sprinkling of storytelling. “There…

events.title: Hilary Hawke Band, Stash Wyslouch
about: The Hilary Hawke Band is a fun, powerhouse quartet featuring guitarist Ross Martin (Jacob Joliff Band, Matt Flinner Trio), fiddler Camille Howes, and bassist Myles Sloniker (Jacob Joliff Band) based out of NYC. Since forming as a trio in 2022, the group has built its identity around improvisation, original songwriting, and a shared love of bluegrass and old-time traditions. Hilary and Ross bring over 15 years of shared musical history across a range of bluegrass projects while also stretching into the world of original music. The band leans into songwriting and improvisation, with performances that are vibrant and engaging. Expect banjo drive, soaring fiddle melodies, intricate guitar work, tasteful bass lines, rich harmonies, all grounded in songs that celebrate creativity, and the joy of being live in a room with an audience.

Stash Wyslouch - Guitarist Stash Wyslouch is hailed as one of bluegrass’s most powerful genre‑bending pioneers—a firebrand whose “sonic kaleidoscope of weirdness and wonder” mixes thrash metal, old‑time, jazz, and classic bluegrass into wildly original, jaw‑dropping music that somehow feels both delightfully zany and deeply soulful.

Stash has played and recorded with Bruce Molsky’s Mountain Drifters, The Jacob Jolliff Band and The Deadly Gentlemen and shared the stage with the likes of Bryan Sutton, Billy Strings, Julian Lage, David Grisman and Peter Rowan.

events.title: Jay Bragg Presents: Christmas in New Vaudeville
about: From Nashville, Jay Bragg's beloved "Christmas in New Vaudeville" returns to The Burren in Somerville, MA bringing The Merriest Show On Earth — now in its 6th annual year — to his home base of New England. Jay, whose grandparents performed in 1930s vaudeville, transforms into bandleader King Kazoo from the North Pole, adorned in his signature bright red frock coat, top hat, brass kazoo, and a dose of whimsy that only the Wizard of Whimsy can muster — leading The Reindeer Band through a joyful, theatrical night of original and holiday music built for the whole family. Equal parts vaudeville throwback and Christmas spectacle, this is a holiday show like you've never experienced and will never forget.

events.title: The Nightflies
about: New selections, first-time by us, from Gaucho, The Nightfly, The Royal Scam, Katy Lied..and more.

A 10-piece band from the Boston/Merrimack Valley area that began as an informal get-together, for the love and challenge of playing the intricate arrangements of Donald Fagen and Walter Becker. Our name is a tip-of-the-hat to the 1982 standard-bearer Donald Fagen solo album,The Nightfly.

The Nightflies perform an ambitious medley of those recognizable, danceable, foot-tapping, 70's-80's hits and plenty of Becker/Fagen's deep-cuts. Hear faves from...Can't Buy a Thrill, Countdown To Ecstasy, Pretzel Logic, Katy Lied, The Royal Scam, Aja, Gaucho, and last but not least Fagen's solo effort, The Nightfly. The Nightflies are available for venues, private parties, and corporate events.

events.title: Matt Heaton’s Burren Boogie: Family Music
about: Matt Heaton’s fun for the whole family kids show residency continues!

Matt Heaton believes music for kids can be entertaining for both children AND parents. His songs blend mid century American guitar styles: surf, rockabilly, western swing & soul, delivered with a wry sense of humor and a sincere sense of fun. Children and adults respond to his musicianship and variety. The grown ups in the room particularly appreciate the Muppet-esque touches of humor and observations of kid behavior. Whether you call it children's music, family music, kindie or toddlerbilly it's sure to please listeners of all ages.

events.title: Torch Light Music School
about: Welcome to Torch Light Music School's 25th Anniversary Show!! Featuring our finest soloists, groups and songwriters from our new SongWrite Class! We're so excited...come celebrate!!

events.title: Brian O’Donovan Legacy Series: Coig Christmas
about: Celebrate the season in style with one of Atlantic Canada’s premiere Celtic supergroups as they take concert goers on a musical journey with their renditions of timeless Christmas classics, brimming instrumentals and high-energy original tunes. An exceptional show from start to finish, Còig brings various influences to their Celtic holiday mix ranging from Folk, Classical, to Swing, giving your favourite carols a fresh and original sound. The quartet features four accomplished multi-instrumentalists and award-winning musicians, Rachel Davis, Darren McMullen, Margie Beaton and Thierry Clouette.

events.title: Fletcheros
about: Fletcheros is the long running cover band based out of the Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy at Tufts, proving that diplomacy nerds can also rock out. From Ariana Grande to Nirvana to The Police, they play it all. Members may be transient, but Fletcheros transcends the test of time.
fletcheros.cover.band/

events.title: Invisible Sun - Featuring The Music of The Police
about: Invisible Sun started 15 years ago when Scott Babineau, Brian Chaffee, and Chris Reddy decided to play some songs by The Police at a jam session. That session turned into an annual event and with the addition last year of drummer Rick Dondero, Invisible Sun has become one of the premier Police cover bands around. They cover 25 songs from The Police, spanning all of their recorded work, with special attention to the detail and stylings of the originals!
Brian Chaffee is an accomplished vocalist/keyboardist from the Gardner area who has fronted "The Franks," "Krakow" and now regularly performs with “Hot Mess”!
Scott Babineau is a fixture in the central Ma music scene as a solo artist, front man for the very popular "Caves on Mars" and session/live work with multiple area musicians, including Mark Marquis.

Chris Reddy, besides being a solo artist performing “Acoustic Loops from Hell," is currently working as the lead guitar player for the band "Doctor Robert" and was the lead singer/ lead guitarist for the Prog rock band "Transit" for 25 years. He has opened for Dave Mason, Gary Hoey, Stan Ridgeway, Jim Weider and Johnny A.

Rick Dondero, who has been playing drums for over 3 decades, has taken the reins as drummer for Invisible Sun. He also plays with Scott in “Caves on Mars” and is currently playing with several other central Ma. bands, as well. An accomplished drummer, Rick pays attention to the essence of Copeland’s ska and jazz elements.
If you enjoy the music of The Police, you must see this show!
Invisible Sun: Brian Chaffee (lead vocals/keyboards) Scott Babineau (bass/lead Vocals) Chris Reddy (lead guitar) Rick Dondero (Drums/Percussion)!

events.title: Opera Untapped : Drunk Opera History: Messiah Sing
about: Join Opera Untapped as we turn the New England Messiah Sing tradition on its head, adding the fun back story about Handel, a little trivia, and a casual atmosphere where you can sing along… with a beer in hand if that’s your vibe. Expect epic vocal soloists, hilarious anecdotes, and a joyful sprinkling of trumpet to tie it all together. By the end of this family-friendly afternoon, we'll have the whole crowd on their feet for a raucous Hallelujah Chorus!

Opera Untapped brings people together through bold, intimate, and innovative performances that showcase the beauty, drama, and humanity of the classical voice. Through immersive productions, interdisciplinary collaborations, and community-centered programming, Opera Untapped creates joyful artistic experiences that surprise, inspire, and connect audiences of all backgrounds. Learn more at

events.title: New England Irish Harp Orchestra - NEIHO
about: The New England Irish Harp Orchestra has been delighting audiences for twenty six years. The Orchestra consists of many harpers, hailing from the New England states, along with fiddle, bodhran, and voices. They have toured in the States and Ireland and have produced four CD’s.
$25 in advance. (+ processing fees) $30 at the door.
This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 6pm. Showtime is 7pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables.

events.title: JGB Tribute, The Diamond Blues
about: Diamond Blues, delivers high-energy, soulful, and exploratory performances in tribute to the one-of-a-kind, rock-gospel-soul-rhythm and blues group, Jerry Garcia Band.
Since 2021, Diamond Blues, an eclectic group of accomplished musicians passionate about honoring the legacy of Jerry Garcia, have taken New England by storm.

Led by David Rubin on Vocals & Guitar, Diamond Blues features Robbie Parrish on Drums, Ian Brenkle on Bass, Caroline Killoh on Vocals & Keys, and Christopher Belden on Sax and backing vocals. An ensemble capable of furnishing any era of the Jerry Garcia Band story.

DB, as it’s often called by fans, mines their repertoire from the Jerry Garcia Band songbook and blends other fan favorites consistent with the original sound of JGB. Their uniquely crafted setlists touch the entire catalogs of JGB, Legion of Mary/Merl Saunders, and Jerry Garcia Solo, leaving audiences inspired and electrified. DB blends deep cuts with hits that will have you respectfully asking, “why didn’t Jerry play that more often?”
$17 in advance. $22 at the door.
This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 7:30. Showtime is 8pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables.

events.title: Brian O'Donovan Legacy Series: Lunasa - TWO SHOWS
about: One of the most influential bands in the history of Irish traditional music, celebrated its twenty fifth anniversary in 2022. Named after an ancient Celtic harvest festival in honour of the Irish god Lugh, the group that Folk Roots magazine once called an “Irish music dream team” was formed from members of some of Ireland’s greatest bands and over the years has proven its mettle time and again, having sold over a quarter of a million records, performed more than 2,000 shows in high-profile concert venues across 36 countries, and collaborated with many notable artists outside the tradition. Two decades ago they ascended to the forefront of contemporary Irish music, and there they’ve remained, a leading voice in the genre and the standard against which others are compared.
“…state-of-the-art Irish music as aggressively infectious as you’ll ever hear.”
– Dirty Linen (2000)

events.title: Brendan Cleary + Wilf: Album Release Show
about: In 2019, Brendan Cleary’s life restarted. After years of struggling with addiction, the world came crashing down. It was the beginning of the road back to finding his voice again.

Playing hotel bars and restaurants, Brendan slowly felt his way back to the songwriter he had always been at heart, connecting with audiences through stories of his struggles and victories. His hard work paid off: Brendan has since been named a finalist in the New Hampshire Music Collective Songwriting Competition, has appeared on NHPR’s The Folk Show with Kate McNally, WSCA’s The Button Factory Soundcheck, and Maine Public Television’s 207 to discuss his story and music. In 2025, Folk legend Tom Rush invited Brendan to tour across the United States as his accompanist.

This December, Brendan releases his debut studio record, Soundbox: an intimate portrait of a songwriter rediscovering his voice through failure, love, and recovery. He joins Wilf at The Burren for a year-end release show celebrating two voices from Cambridge’s songwriting scene.

Wilf is a Boston-based singer-songwriter whose introspective music blends droning indie folk with traditional ballads. Often using alternate tunings, his songs carry an ominous quality that, paired with poetic lyrics, attempt to transfer personal ruminations onto the audience for self-reflection. His debut EP, Pity, releases November 13, 2026, and draws inspiration from artists including Ethel Cain, Elliott Smith, and Slowdive. The EP dissects the transition into adulthood, examining feelings of stagnation and self-pity.

events.title: The Nervous Eaters with Special Guest Geoff Abraham Band
about: The Nervous Eaters are an original rock and roll band from Boston, MA who helped define the Boston underground garage/punk rock scene of the late 70’s.
Geoff Abraham Band delivers high-energy bluesy rock 'n' roll with infectious hooks, unforgettable melodies, and plenty of swagger..
$25 in advance. $30 at the door.
This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 6pm. Showtime is 6:30pm.

events.title: A Charlie Brown Christmas
about: Come experience the magic of the season as a live jazz piano trio brings A Charlie Brown Christmas to life on stage! This heartwarming performance captures the nostalgic charm of Vince Guaraldi’s iconic soundtrack, featuring beloved tunes like “Linus and Lucy,” “Christmas Time Is Here,” and more. Performed with improvised, authentic arrangements and the warm energy of live musicianship, this show is a joyful celebration for all ages—perfect for fans of Snoopy, jazz lovers, and anyone who wants to embrace the holiday spirit. Bring your friends and family for an unforgettable day of timeless music and festive cheer!

events.title: Jazz Composers Alliance Orchestra in Concert
about: The Jazz Composers Alliance Orchestra presents the music of faculty members Bob Pilkington, Dave Harris, Mimi Rabson, and Darrell Katz in concert.

events.title: Emperor's New Clothes
about: The Emperor's New Clothes is a musical adaptation for family audiences based on the classic tale, written by Berklee Theater Arts Collaborative Artistic Director Rene Pfister, and featuring the Theater for Young Audiences Ensemble.

events.title: The Canadian Arabic Orchestra: Nightingale
about: Nightingale celebrates the romance, nostalgia, and timeless beauty of Arabic music’s golden era.

events.title: Singers Night: Journey—Don't Stop Believin'
about: Each semester, 250 talented Berklee College of Music vocal students audition for a coveted spot in Singers Night, one of the Voice Department’s most prestigious showcases. This semester, they present the music of Journey.

events.title: A Celebration of Hip-Hop: Berklee Hip-Hop Hall of Fame Inducts Big Daddy Kane
about: Join the Berklee community for A Celebration of Hip-Hop, an extraordinary evening presented by the Berklee Africana Studies Division, bringing together legendary pioneers and the next generation of musical innovators.

events.title: Pooh: La Nostra Storia North America Tour 2026
about: Experience the legendary Italian pop-rock band Pooh live for the final time in North America as they celebrate 60 years of iconic music in a once-in-a-lifetime farewell.

events.title: Coltrane 100: Both Directions at Once
about: 2026 marks the centennial of John Coltrane's birth. Coltrane 100 brings together saxophonists Joe Lovano and Melissa Aldana, pianist Leo Genovese, bassist Linda May Han Oh, and drummer Jeff "Tain" Watts for a collective tribute to Coltrane's enduring influence.

events.title: Singers Showcase: Forever Whitney Houston
about: Berklee’s Singers Showcase presents Forever Whitney Houston, a celebration of the artistry, performance, and legacy of one of the greatest singers of all time, featuring a global student cast.

events.title: Singers Showcase: Forever Whitney Houston
about: Berklee’s Singers Showcase presents Forever Whitney Houston, a celebration of the artistry, performance, and legacy of one of the greatest singers of all time, featuring a global student cast.

events.title: Holiday Spectacular: Nutcracker Suite with Diamond Cut Big Band
about: This two-part concert features arrangements of holiday songs performed by the Gen-Next All-Stars, and Duke Ellington's Nutcracker Suite performed by the Diamond Cut Big Band.

events.title: Berklee City Music High School Academy Winter Showcase Concert
about: The Berklee City Music High School Academy Winter Showcase Concert features seven ensembles performing various musical styles and arrangements.

events.title: The 8-Bit Big Band: The Great Video Game Songbook
about: The 8-Bit Big Band is a Grammy Award–winning contemporary symphonic jazz orchestra created to celebrate and reimagine the most beloved music from video game history.

events.title: FORMIDABLE! Aznavour: The Story of a Legend
about: FORMIDABLE! Aznavour: The Story of a Legend, is far more than a tribute concert. It is a moving journey through the life, music, passion, and extraordinary international career of the legendary performer Charles Aznavour, whose songs touched millions around the world.

events.title: MIT Henge 2026
about: Observe the sun as it aligns with the Infinite Corridor!

Tuesday, November 10, at approximately 4:19:23 pm Light refreshments to follow in Lobby 13 Watch Professor Post-Tenure Richard Binzel explain this unique piece of MIT's lore in this video short about MIT Henge!

Warning: The fact that the sun is at the horizon does not mean that it is safe to look at for more than a moment. Do not injure your eyes by staring at the sun. Use appropriate filters or glance only for a moment as you would at the sun up in the sky.
View from the Building 8 end. Don’t go up to the Building 7/Mass. Ave. end of the corridor. You won’t see anything special there, and you will prevent others from seeing.

Arrive early and don’t block the corridor. Especially given the apparent systematic tendency for predictions to be 5-8 minutes late, it’s best to arrive 15 minutes early. This helps make sure you’re not trying to scramble for a spot and blocking somebody else’s view. Above all, do not walk in the corridor in front of all the people trying to catch a glimpse of the sun.

Don’t leave until the very end. People who take a picture in the middle and then leave block the corridor for those still observing. Some people observe for the entire span in which the sun is even barely visible; leaving early blocks their view.

Use the third floor. The 3rd floor has the best view because it has an uninterrupted sweep of corridor, and because it is the highest usable floor. You can’t see anything from the fourth floor because it doesn’t go through.
Let others see. Not very many people can get a good view of this phenomenon at once. Once you have seen, get out of the way and let others look.

Stand in the stairwell. The place that has the largest unobstructed angle of view of the sky is the stairwell just below the third floor. Get your eye right by the edge of corridor floor. Great view? Now give someone else a chance.
Don’t hurt your eyes. See the warning above.
Read more info on Infinite Corridor astronomy!

about: History at MIT invites you to join us on Thursday, November 19th at 5 pm in E51-095 for the final lecture in the History of Now series, featuring Orit Bashkin, the Mabel Greene Myers Professor of Modern Middle Eastern History and Director of Graduate Studies, Modern Fields at the University of Chicago. Her talk is titled "A Different Critique: MENA Jewish Approaches to Zionism and Imperialism, 1830-1948."
Mabel Greene Myers Professor of Modern Middle Eastern History Director of Graduate Studies, Modern Fields University of Chicago Thursday, November 19, 2026
5-6:30 pm · MIT Building E51, Room 095

Orit Bashkin is a historian who works on the intellectual, social, and cultural history of the modern Middle East. She got her Ph.D. from Princeton University (2004), writing a thesis on Iraqi intellectual history under the supervision of Professors Robert Tignor and Samah Selim, and her BA (1995) and MA (1999) from Tel Aviv University. Since her graduation, she has been working as a professor of modern Middle Eastern history in the Department of Near Eastern Languages and Civilizations at the University of Chicago. Her publications deal with Iraqi history, the history of Iraqi Jews, the Arab cultural revival movement (the nahda) in the late 19th century, and the connections between modern Arab history and Arabic literature. Her current research project explores the lives of Iraqi Jews in Israel.

events.title: MIT Music Tech Speaker Series Presents: Mark Ethier
about: Tools for Musicians in the Age of AI: From iZotope to Berklee Music and technology have always co-evolved. Long before the synthesizer, innovations ranging from new tuning systems to the piano's sustain pedal haven’t just made music easier to produce — they’ve fundamentally changed what kind of music is possible to make. How will AI as an underlying technology fit into this history?

Since I was an undergraduate at MIT, I’ve spent my career building tools for musicians and watching this interplay firsthand. Sometimes, new technology inspires the music itself, like how rhythmic delay helped inspire U2’s “Where the Streets Have No Name.” Other times, musicians drive the technology. At iZotope, our collaboration with BT on Stutter Edit took intricate audio effects that could require hours of studio editing and made them playable in real time onstage.

I’ve also witnessed the impact of the democratization of music making. We helped build a path for musicians to launch careers from their bedrooms, but we also watched large-format studios close their doors. It’s too early to fully grasp how generative AI will impact creative possibilities and livelihoods, but I'll share some early signals from recent market research, including Berklee’s June 2026 report, In Sync: Music and Video 2026.

Now, we’re entering a new phase: the democratization of tool building. With a quiet revolution of musicians vibe-coding their own tools, this story is far from over. In these moments of change, it’s often clear what is being lost. But we also have to wonder what new artistic expression becomes possible, and with the evolution of generative AI, question who gets to shape that change and benefit from it.

Mark Ethier is an entrepreneur and innovator dedicated to empowering creativity. In 2001, after graduating from MIT with degrees in music and computer science, he cofounded iZotope. Today, he is the Founding Executive Director of Berklee's Emerging Artistic Technology Lab (BEATL) helping musicians navigate technology.

Under Mark’s leadership as CEO, iZotope’s tools helped musicians, engineers, and producers realize their creative vision and earned numerous honors, including multiple NAMM TEC Awards (Technical Excellence & Creativity), two Primetime Engineering Emmy Awards for Outstanding Achievement in Engineering Development, and an Academy Award for Scientific and Engineering Achievement.…

events.title: Author Talk: A Pox on Fools
about: Join us for an engaging evening with author Thomas Levenson as he discusses his new book, "A Pox on Fools: The True Believers, Grifters, and Cynics Who Convinced Us to Reject Vaccines," in conversation with MIT Museum Director Michael John Gorman.

Since the advent of smallpox inoculation in the eighteenth century, the idea that a disease introduced to the body in some lesser, weakened form might prevent full-blown infection has been one of the greatest public health insights of the modern era, inspiring the invention of numerous vaccines and saving countless human lives. But, just as humanity acquired the superhuman ability to stop infectious disease in its tracks, some feared we had gone too far, leading to skepticism that has hijacked public health discourse today.

In three sweeping essays written for our current moment of scientific mistrust, Thomas Levenson searches for the origins of the most common arguments against vaccines: that they are unnatural; that they are more dangerous than the illnesses they claim to prevent; and that they are an affront to freedom. Each arose from the earliest development of particular vaccines and the campaigns to distribute them. Even as the pattern repeats, Levenson reveals how innocent that skepticism initially was and, in each case, how very human fears and questions ultimately turned into something darker, where no truth would be enough to overcome the doubt.

events.title: Co-Adaptive—Ruth Mandl and Bobby Johnston
about: Part of the MIT Fall 2026 Architecture Lecture Series Presented with the Architecture and Urbanism Group As our planet gets hotter, and more extreme weather events become the norm, CO Adaptive is positioning themselves as an unbuild, design and build practice: a new model that reunites designers and builders through collaboration in order to re-think our joint role in shaping the built environment; contending with architecture at the intersection of saving embodied carbon and reducing operational energy. As stewards of the existing material repository contained in our cities, CO Adaptive aims to increase the resilience and reusability of all that already surrounds us.

Their talk will engage the breadth of the practice’s work—from adaptive reuse projects and high-efficiency retrofits to material salvage operations, remanufacturing, and design for disassembly. These projects yield a critical perspective on how buildings and materials re-engage in their next iteration of use, working towards a reality in which extractive and depleting habits are replaced by a circular library of abundance.

CO Adaptive is an unbuild-design-build practice founded by Ruth Mandl and Bobby Johnston in 2011. Initially it was started as an architecture practice, focused on retrofitting existing building stock to create energy efficient, climate resilient and spatially beautiful environments.

To have a greater impact on the process of taking old buildings apart—emphasizing deconstruction, and shaping attitudes about “waste”—CO Adaptive Building was established in 2021 and CO Adaptive Disassembly in 2026. The attention of all three intertwined practices is on converting existing buildings from a linear economy to a circular one.

CO Adaptive’s work has received numerous awards and recognition, including winning the Architectural League’s Emerging Voices 2026, A|N’s 2025 Best of Practice Award, and the 2025 Trust for Governors Island Climate Solutions Challenge. Their adaptive reuse project for The Mercury Store was featured in MoMA’s Inaugural New York New Publics exhibition and won the MASterworks Design Award for Adaptive Reuse in 2023. Ruth and Bobby are frequent lecturers on circular design, have taught a graduate design studio at Columbia GSAPP, and are excited to be teaching a studio at MIT this fall.

about: Join us for a special conversation with author Ted Chiang and MIT President Sally Kornbluth about Exhalation. President Kornbluth has chosen Chiang’s celebrated science fiction short story collection to celebrate 10 years of MIT Reads. Exploring the book’s provocative questions about technology and humanity, their discussion will focus on the stories "The Truth of Fact, the Truth of Feeling,” "The Lifecycle of Software Objects,” “Omphalos,” “What’s Expected of Us," and "Exhalation."

In this fantastical and elegant collection, Chiang wrestles with the oldest questions on Earth – What is the nature of the universe? What does it mean to be human? – and ones that no one else has even imagined. And, each in its own way, the stories prove that complex and thoughtful science fiction can rise to new heights of beauty, meaning, and compassion.

This event is part of MIT Reads, a program that embraces the power of reading and storytelling to cultivate social connection, individual reflection, and a sense of our shared humanity. Designed to foster empathy, curiosity, and belonging, MIT Reads brings together the campus community – and readers everywhere – through common reading experiences, author talks, and group discussions.
This hybrid event is free and open to all, but pre-registration is required. For online participants, the URL will be emailed closer to the event.

events.title: Author Talk: Sandy Bailey - She's On to Something
about: Sandy Bailey joins us to discuss her debut novel She’s On to Something. When hard-charging SEC prosecutor Jaye Brannigan stumbles onto a church-based investment scam draining millions from working-class families, she knows the case could make—or end—her career.

Queer, outspoken, and already targeted by a hostile administration, Jaye follows the money from Boston to New Mexico, uncovering a web of religious patriarchy, financial fraud, and offshore secrets. As the danger mounts, so does the temptation to guard her heart—especially when a magnetic woman pulls her toward connection just as everything else threatens to unravel.

Sandy will appear in conversation with her wife, Liz Nania, the inspiration for the character of Rose. This program is presented in partnership with Rozzie Bound. This program is presented in partnership with Rozzie Bound. Copies of the book will be available to purchase at the event.

Sandy Bailey has been a freight and passenger train engineer, a carpenter, and a prosecutor before building a career investigating white-collar crime in New Mexico, Boston, and Washington, D.C. Her experience uncovering financial fraud informs the high-stakes world of her fiction. She lives in Boston, where she organizes community events, explores local trails, plays basketball with her lesbian hoops squad, and shares a love of queer dance with her wife.

events.title: Author Talk: Laura Zigman — The Author Weekend
about: The Fall 2026 Author Talk Series, presented by the Friends of the South End Library, will continue with Laura Zigman sharing about her latest novel, The Author Weekend. Please join us on Wednesday, November 11 starting at 6:30 pm at Union Church (Connection Room, 485 Columbus Ave.) for a fun and lively conversation in this author talk series!

Everything needs to be just right for bestselling mystery writer Faye Wader's first ever fan weekend. Her sales might be slipping––only a little!––but her readers still love her enough to pony up for three days and two nights on Great Misery Island. The retreat is precisely planned, from the small batch artisanal donuts to the perimenopausal Mermaid Meditation, by Faye and her beleaguered assistant Jade––an aspiring author who can't seem to finish her own novel. Faye's long-time agent and editor will be there, as well as Faye's number one fan, Peggy Mercer, who has been first in line at every one of Faye's events. When news comes that the weekend will be crashed by glamorous, charismatic, rival novelist Abby Schuss, Faye thinks things can't get worse... until one of the attendees is found dead in her room, setting off an unexpectedly murderous chain of events that make pre-pub anxiety seem like a day at the beach. How far is Faye willing to go to get exactly what she wants from her author weekend? The Author Weekend is a thrilling and hilarious dive into the dark heart of envy, and a glorious exploration of a woman of a certain age desperate to survive the dog-eat-dog world of publishing and control her own narrative.

Laura Zigman is the author of Small World, Separation Anxiety, Animal Husbandry, Dating Big Bird, Her, and Piece of Work. She has collaborated on several works of nonfiction—including Eddie Izzard’s New York Times bestseller, Believe Me—and has been a contributor to The New York Times and other publications.

events.title: Art Exhibition — Rachel King: At the Water's Edge
about: The Jamaica Plain Branch Library, in partnership with the Friends of the Jamaica Plain Branch of the Boston Public Library, is pleased to present At the Water’s Edge, the next exhibition of its 2026 rotating art series, featuring photography by Jamaica Plain artist Rachel King.

At the Water’s Edge traces the seasonal shifts along the shore of Jamaica Pond. Working in the field of addiction and recovery, King began turning to photography in the wake of the overdose epidemic, intensified by COVID-19, as a way to connect more deeply with her local landscape and community. What began as documenting the familiar evolved into a daily photographic journal, an exercise in slowing down and paying attention to small changes that can easily go unnoticed.

King was drawn to the water’s edge, where waves, melting ice, changing light, and reflections continually alter the landscape, transforming recognizable forms into unexpected patterns and abstract shapes.The daily practice also became a way of marking time. Each image captures conditions that may never recur in quite the same way; together, they form a record not only of a changing landscape, but of the act of looking itself.

Through At the Water’s Edge, King invites viewers to look closely at a place that may already feel familiar, and to consider how sustained attention can reveal new ways of seeing even a landscape we know well.

At the Water’s Edge is on view from November 12, 2026–January 6, 2027, with a public reception to be held on Thursday, November 12, 2026, 5:30-7:30 PM. The library is open Monday-Wednesday 10-6, Thursday 12-8, and Friday and Saturday 9-5 (closed Sundays). The exhibition space is located on the lower level.

This exhibition is made possible through the generous support of The Friends of the Jamaica Plain Branch Library, a volunteer, community-based organization that seeks to enhance public awareness, recognition, status and financial support of the library system through advocacy and education.

events.title: Author Talk: Lauren Klein and Tanvi Sharma on "Data by Design"
about: Join visualization historian Lauren Klein and designer Tanvi Sharma for a conversation about their new book Data by Design: Visualization and Power from Abolition to the Dawn of Data Science. The book returns to the history of data visualization to expose the power of charts and maps—and to show how they can be used for social change. Lauren and Tanvi will be in conversation with Arvind Satyanarayan, a professor of data visualization at MIT.

​Lauren Klein is Professor of Data & Decision Sciences and English at Emory University, where she also directs the Digital Humanities Lab and the Atlanta Interdisciplinary AI Network. Her research brings together computational and critical methods to explore questions of gender, race, and justice, both in early America and today. Klein is the author (with Catherine D’Ignazio) of the award-winning Data Feminism (MIT Press, 2020), and the editor (with Matthew K. Gold) of Debates in the Digital Humanities (Univ. of Minnesota Press), among other publications.

​Tanvi Sharma is a design technologist working at the intersection of data, aesthetics, and the humanities. She is currently an Art Director at Apple and co-author of Data by Design (MIT Press, 2026). She has previously worked at Pentagram, Public Policy Lab, and Spotify. She lives in Harlem, NY, with her two cats, Yuchi and Bubbles. More at tanvi.network.

​Arvind Satyanarayan is an Associate Professor of Computer Science at MIT EECS, and leads the Visualization Group at the Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Lab (CSAIL). His research uses visualization as a petri dish to study intelligence augmentation (IA), or how computation can amplify our cognition and creativity, while respecting our agency. Open-source visualization systems developed by Arvind and his collaborators are widely used by researchers, companies, and journalists. Arvind’s research has been recognized with several awards including, most recently, an Alfred P. Sloan Fellowship.

events.title: Before Salem: Witchcraft in Boston’s North End, 1688: Cotton Mather, Martha Goodwin, and the Making of a Witchcraft Panic
about: Join the Friends of the North End Branch Library in welcoming James Pasto for Before Salem: Witchcraft in Boston’s North End, 1688: Cotton Mather, Martha Goodwin, and the Making of a Witchcraft Panic.

In 1688, Boston’s North End was the scene of one of New England’s most famous witchcraft cases. Four children of the Goodwin family were believed to have been bewitched, and Cotton Mather, one of Boston’s leading Puritan ministers, became closely involved in the case. This talk examines the Goodwin case within the broader history of Puritan Boston and the beliefs, fears, and social tensions that shaped accusations of witchcraft. Drawing on insights from cultural anthropology, it explores how witchcraft beliefs function in different societies, why accusations arise, and how the events in Boston helped set the stage for the Salem witchcraft trials of 1692.
Presented by James S. Pasto, Ph.D.

events.title: Author Talk — Alex Krieger: Greenhorn
about: Join local author Alex Krieger as he reads from and discusses his new memoir Greenhorn: Episodes in an Immigrant's Life. It explores a life shaped by motion, memory, cultures and careers, which unfolds in the art of making a home in the unfamiliar. At the age of nine, Alex Krieger arrived in America with his three parents—survivors of the Holocaust. In Chicago, he finds his fourth first-grade classroom to learn a fourth language in four years. From displaced childhood, the journeying continues as teacher, architect, planner of cities. With a poet's sensitivity and a craftsman's precision, Krieger reflects on that greenhorn's instinct to embrace the values of an adopted nation while remaining eyewitness to paradoxes.

Alex Krieger is Professor Emeritus at the Harvard Graduate School of Design where he taught since 1977. An architect, planner and author, he has directed design and planning projects in American and international cities, including the reconstruction of the Bund in Shanghai. Former chair of the Department of Urban Planning and Design, he remains an advisor to public and educational institutions, including two terms on the U.S. Commission of Fine Arts. He is a founding board member of the Leventhal Map & Education Center and the co-author of Mapping Boston.

events.title: Author Talk: Paul Lewis — How "The Raven" Became America's Most Famous Poem
about: Join Boston College Professor Emeritus Paul Lewis in a discussion of his new book on Edgar Allan Poe's famous poem.

In 1845, over 5,300 poems were published in American magazines. Most immediately began their deserved descent into oblivion. Poe's "Raven" stands as the most conspicuous exception to this. But why? What factors influenced the attention devoted to "The Raven" from the day when it was first published? Why was it widely reprinted, praised, criticized, and mocked during the next weeks and months? Why did it inspire parodies that replaced Poe's "saintly bird of yore" with a veritable menagerie of other animals—including an owl, gazelle, turkey, pig, dog, cats, rats, and (eek!) bedbugs? And how did Poe's reputation—as a literary brawler and harsh book reviewer and as a man who struggled with money and alcohol—play into the reception of "The Raven"? Signed copies of Paul Lewis' Quothing "The Raven" The First Responses to America's Most Famous Poem will be available at this book-launch event.

Paul Lewis is a Professor Emeritus at Boston College, a past president of the Poe Studies Association, and the curator of exhibitions on literary Boston. As the Board of Directors chair of the Edgar Allan Poe Foundation of Boston, Inc., Lewis worked with others to celebrate Poe in the city of his birth by having a square at the intersection of Boylston Street and Charles Street South dedicated to Poe in 2010 and then installing a statue of Poe in it in 2014.

events.title: The Boston Symphony Orchestra and ICA/Boston present Sudan Archives: Any Shape I Want
about: *Tickets for this performance are sold out.

Sudan Archives brings a new performance to the Institute of Contemporary Art/Boston in a co-production with the Boston Symphony Orchestra as part of the BSO’s Creation Festival. The New York Times has called her “an artist in a league of her own,” and Pitchfork praised her “thrillingly original” fusion of sound and storytelling.
$25 ICA members and students / $30 nonmembers <div

events.title: The Artist’s Voice: Leilah Babirye with Ruth Erickson
about: “Reusing materials is important to me, as a person who comes from a background where the LGBTQ community is looked at as trash still today. As an artist, I find beauty in using found materials to showcase and reclaim my community.” -Leilah Babirye Bicycle chains, gears, and tire tubes are some of the unexpected elements in Leilah Babirye’s latest sculptures at the ICA. Her art, celebrating a one-of-a-kind queer wedding, depicts attendees of this special life event through ceramic and carved wood sculptures. Join Babirye and ICA’s Barbara Lee Chief Curator Ruth Erickson as they reflect on the artist’s unique practice that proudly reclaims space, identity, and community through art. This program explores Babirye’s many creative influences from African sculpture to found object art and addresses cultural and political systems of oppression embedded in Uganda, including the Anti-Homosexuality Act (2014/2023) that endangers and criminalizes many lives.
An exhibition publication signing will follow the talk. Books will be available for purchase at the event.
Free

events.title: Bill T. Jones/Arnie Zane Company: Collage Revisited and Story/
about: The Bill T. Jones/Arnie Zane Company return to the ICA with a program reflecting on history, legacy, and continued experimentation.

As recently announced by New York Live Arts, the internationally acclaimed Company will bring its 45-year history of performance and touring to a close in December 2027. This engagement offers Boston audiences one of the final opportunities to experience the Company live before its final season.
$45 ICA members / $50 students / $60 nonmembers

events.title: Gallery Talk: Max Gruber on 90 YEARS
about: Founded in 1936, the ICA is one of the oldest museums dedicated to contemporary art in the United States. On this special anniversary, 90 YEARS revisits nine exhibitions and initiatives from the ICA’s history, tracing the museum’s evolution alongside the ever-changing landscape of contemporary art. Join Curatorial Assistant Max Gruber for a conversation about pivotal moments in the ICA’s history with a focus on the landmark 1941 exhibition Modern Mexican Painters.

Max Gruber is Curatorial Assistant at the Institute of Contemporary Art/Boston. He has contributed to several ICA exhibitions, including Tau Lewis: Spirit Level, The Gun Violence Memorial Project, Charles Atlas: About Time, and An Indigenous Present. Before joining the ICA, Gruber contributed to the exhibition and accompanying publication for Humane Ecology: Eight Positions at the Clark Art Institute. He holds an M.A. in the History of Art from Williams College.
Free with museum admission <div

about: Join us on November 14th to watch A World of 3 Zeros and stay after for a Zoom Q&A with the Co-Directors, Áine Clark and Michel Van Der Veken.

Poverty, unemployment, and carbon emissions are global problems. A World of 3 Zeros explores the ability of social entrepreneurship to address these issues and bring them to zero. This documentary takes the audience on the journey undertaken by filmmakers Áine and Michel, to shed light on the works of this new type of business. A concept purposely designed to address social and environmental problems with entrepreneurs who joyfully aim for impact over profit maximization, with solutions that can be shared or adopted elsewhere in the world for the common good.

ÁINE CLARKE (born 1963, Belfast, Northern Ireland) Graduated from the University of Ulster with a degree in Environmental Physics in 1987. Until 2016, Áine served as the commercial and marketing business developer for Azimut Company, building client relationships and managing business growth. Her passion for listening, and commitment to authentic representation though storytelling drives her approach to documentary filmmaking.

MICHEL VAN DER VEKEN (born 1961, Liège, Belgium) Graduate of L'IAD Film Institution (1985). Michel brings technical precision and creative vision developed through 25 years of commercial filmmaking to documentary work. His cinematography reveals the humanity in each subject while creating visual cohesion across diverse global settings.

events.title: Behind the Screen: La Bola Negra
about: LA BOLA NEGRA, the bold new film from Spanish writer-directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, won the Best Director award at Cannes and the People's Choice award at the Toronto International Film Festival. Inspired by the surviving pages of an unfinished play by Federico García Lorca and by Alberto Conejero's award-winning play La piedra oscura, the film tells the interconnected stories of three gay men in Spain in 1932, 1937, and 2017. Moving from the years before the Spanish Civil War, through the war itself, to the present day, LA BOLA NEGRA is a sweeping, passionate triptych about desire, repression, historical memory, and what one generation carries forward to the next.
Our panel will explore the film's roots in Lorca's work, its portrayal of the Spanish Civil War and the Franco era, and how it brings queer history and historical memory to the screen.

Margaret E. Deffenbaugh and LeRoy T. Carlson Professor in Comparative Literary Studies and Professor of Spanish, Wellesley College Carlos Ramos's teaching and research focus on the literature and cultural history of contemporary Spain. His published work includes Construyendo la modernidad: Escritura y arquitectura en el Madrid moderno (1918-1937) and Poesía insomne.

Associate Professor of Hispanic Studies, Boston College Wan Sonya Tang teaches courses on Spanish literature and culture from the nineteenth century onward. She is the author of Specters, Monsters, and the Damned: Fantastic Threats to the Social Order in 19th-Century Spain and co-editor of Televising Restoration Spain, which examines how heritage film and television explore Spain's relationship to modernity in the late 1800s and early 1900s.
Professor of Hispanic Studies and Comparative Literature, Brandeis University Fernando Rosenberg is the author of After Human Rights: Literature, Visual Arts, and Film in Latin America, 1990-2010.
Directed by Javier Ambrossi, Javier Calvo · 2h 35m

events.title: Behind the Screen: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
about: ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM captures an extraordinary evening in 1972, when pioneering documentarian William Greaves gathered surviving luminaries of the Harlem Renaissance at Duke Ellington's Harlem townhouse. Over four hours, artists, writers, and intellectuals, many of whom had not seen one another in fifty years, reminisced, argued, laughed, and debated their place in a rapidly changing cultural landscape. Greaves considered it the most important event he ever filmed. Decades later, his son David Greaves, one of the original camera operators, restored the 16mm footage and completed the film, creating both a vivid time capsule and a searching inquiry into one of the most creative periods in American history.

Our panelists will discuss the Harlem Renaissance and its legacy, the remarkable figures gathered in Greaves's footage, and the story of how this film was made and, fifty years later, finally completed.

Kendra Taira Field is the Gerald R. Gill Associate Professor of History and Director of the Center for Public History at Tufts University; and a 2025-26 Hutchins Fellow at Harvard University. A citizen of the Muscogee (Creek) Nation, Field is the author of Growing Up with the Country (Yale, 2018), which traced her own ancestors’ post emancipation lives in Indian Territory and Oklahoma. Field’s American Historical Review article, "The Privilege of Family History" explores the history of African American engagement with family history and genealogy in slavery and freedom. Field abridged David Levering Lewis' W.E.B. Du Bois: A Biography (Henry Holt, 2009) and co-founded the Du Bois Forum, a retreat for writers, scholars, and artists. Field serves as Chief Historian for the 10 Million Names Project and has appeared in numerous historical documentaries and television programs, including Henry Louis Gates, Jr.'s "The African Americans: Many Rivers to Cross" (2013) and HBO Max’s, Breaking New Ground

Professor of the Practice, Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies, Tufts University Khary Jones is Professor of the Practice, Theatre, Dance, and Performance Studies at Tufts University. As a writer-director, his work includes the award-winning documentary Night Fight and the short films Hug, Three and a Half Thoughts, and Chrysalis. events.title: Riverdogs & The Same River Twice
about: In 1978 Robb Moss filmed a group of friends, young river guides, on a 35-day rafting trip through the Grand Canyon, and he has kept filming them ever since.

THE SAME RIVER TWICE (2003, 78 min.) catches up with five of those friends, Barry, Cathy, Danny, Jeff and Jim, twenty years later. Two have served as mayors and one as a county commissioner, and all five are weighing the free lives they once led against the ones they have built. The film premiered at the Sundance Film Festival.
RIVERDOGS (1982, 32 min.) is Moss's original record of that summer on the Colorado River, a lyrical and unselfconscious portrait of youth and the canyon. RIVERDOGS contains nudity.

events.title: Riverdogs & The Bend in the River
about: In 1978 Robb Moss filmed a group of friends, young river guides, on a 35-day rafting trip through the Grand Canyon, and he has kept filming them ever since.
RIVERDOGS (1982, 32 min.) is Moss's original 16mm record of that summer on the Colorado River, a lyrical and unselfconscious portrait of youth and the canyon. RIVERDOGS contains nudity.

THE BEND IN THE RIVER (2025, 83 min.) returns to Barry, Cathy, Danny, Jeff and Jim, now in their seventies. Moss weaves together footage from across their lives into a portrait of friendship and aging that is often funny and finally very moving. Executive produced by Frances McDormand and Joel Coen, the film premiered at the 2025 Telluride Film Festival.
Robb Moss joins Anne Marie Stein to talk about filming the same people across a lifetime, and what it is like to watch his friends, and himself, grow older on screen.

Rudolf Arnheim Lecturer on Filmmaking, Harvard University Robb Moss is a documentary filmmaker who teaches filmmaking at Harvard. His films include RIVERDOGS, THE SAME RIVER TWICE, which premiered at Sundance, and SECRECY and CONTAINMENT, both made with Peter Galison. He has been an advisor at the Sundance Institute Documentary Labs since their first year and has served on documentary juries at Sundance and many other festivals.

Former Executive Director, Boston Film/Video Foundation Anne Marie Stein is a Newton resident who led the Boston Film/Video Foundation from 1988 to 2001 and co-founded the Boston International Festival of Women's Cinema.

events.title: Local Spotlight: Cut To David
about: Join us for a one-day only community screening of Cut to David followed by a post-film discussion with the filmmaker Sandy Jaffe and family, and other participants in the film.

David’s story is beautifully layered from the start: An adopted, Chinese-American, transgender teen, raised in a Jewish home in Boston with a filmmaker for a mom, with a camera always close by. As David journeys from high school to college to adulthood, Sandy Jaffe’s camera documents her family’s evolving relationship as each participant has a turn steering the narrative. Blending vérité footage, home videos, and candid conversations, the film begins as an effort to understand David’s gender transition and expands into a deeper exploration of identity, agency, authorship, power, and the complicated yet loving bond between a mother and her son. An intimate, fly-on-the-wall documentary, CUT TO DAVID considers the possibilities—and perils—of living visibly and openly, exploring how ethnicity, gender, religion, and parenting shape who we become.

Sandy Jaffe is a filmmaker and writer, and has taught screenwriting at various institutions in the Boston area. Her first documentary feature, Our Mockingbird, was a part of the PBS series America Reframed. She is a co-facilitator of a parent support group through Greater Boston PFLAG. Cut to David, her second feature documentary, premiered to a sold out audience at GlobeDocs 2026.

Jay Blitzman is a former public defender who specialized in representing youth and late teens. He served for 24 years as a juvenile court judge, retiring as the First Justice of the Middlesex Division of the MA Juvenile Court. He teaches law, consults on youth and criminal issues, and advocates for supporting youth voice and agency in all contexts.

David Blitzman graduated Magna Cum Laude from Ithaca College in 2020. He received his MSW in 2025 from Smith College School of Social Work, and works as a therapist in Greater Boston. David also volunteers for organizations which promote community engagement and collaboration.

events.title: Wild Horse Nine
about: Shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, CIA agents Chris (John Malkovich) and Lee (Sam Rockwell) are dispatched from Santiago to Easter island by their bureau chief, MJ (Steve Buscemi). Amongst the Island's iconic statues, and as the longtime partners wrestle with their dark pasts and present conspiracies, Chris's newfound bond with a pair of rebellious students (Mariana di Girolamo and Ailín Salas) threatens to send everyone’s trip to this remote paradise sideways.
Directed by Martin McDonagh · 1h 58m

events.title: National Theatre Live Golden Boy
about: 1930s New York, at the height of the Depression. Joe Bonaparte is a gifted young violinist with extraordinary talent and a future in music, until a chance at fame and fortune lures him into the brutal world of professional boxing. Pressured by a ruthless manager, tempted by a forbidden love, and bound by the expectations of his Italian-American family, Joe is a young man torn between the seductive promise of the American Dream and the quiet honor of a decent life. He must confront what he’s willing to sacrifice, who he’s willing to become, and how to find his place in a world that demands he choose a side. Sam Yates directs Josh O'Connor in this searing revival of Clifford Odets' knockout American classic. Brought to life with a live string quartet, this propulsive drama explores ambition, identity, and the high price of success.
